lines.zh: 我沿着货架走，数今天少了几块铁。
lines.en: I walk the shelves, counting the iron missing today.

lines.zh: 脚下叮当响，是我腰上的秤砣。
lines.en: My steps clink with the weights hanging at my belt.

lines.zh: 我去后仓看看，货该补了。
lines.en: I head to the back room; the stock needs refilling.

lines.zh: 我走路很慢，怕碰倒堆着的锭。
lines.en: I walk slowly, afraid to topple the stacked ingots.

lines.zh: 每走一圈，我就往账上加一笔。
lines.en: Each lap around the shop, I add a line to the ledger.

lines.zh: 我踩着木地板，声音像在数钱。
lines.en: My boots on the boards sound like counting coins.

lines.zh: 我绕开地上的铜块，那还没标价。
lines.en: I step around the copper; it has no price yet.

lines.zh: 我走到门口，看看有没有客人。
lines.en: I walk to the door to see whether a customer came.

lines.zh: 我边走边掂手里的锭，估个价。
lines.en: I walk while weighing an ingot and guessing its price.

lines.zh: 通道太窄，我得侧着身子过去。
lines.en: The aisle is narrow; I have to turn sideways.

lines.zh: 我走得很稳，这店里没有余地。
lines.en: I walk carefully; this shop has no room to spare.

lines.zh: 我巡到最里一排，灰落了一层。
lines.en: I reach the back row, where a layer of dust has settled.

lines.zh: 我不跑，跑起来会掉铜板。
lines.en: I never run; running spills copper coins.

lines.zh: 我回到柜台前，那里才是我的位置。
lines.en: I return behind the counter, where I belong.

lines.zh: 我用袖子擦一枚旧锭，擦出光。
lines.en: I polish an old ingot with my sleeve until it shines.

lines.zh: 账本上有一笔，我一直算不平。
lines.en: One entry in my ledger has never balanced.

lines.zh: 我把铜板和铁锭分开摆，摆得整齐。
lines.en: I sort copper and iron into two neat stacks.

lines.zh: 我数了一遍库存，又数一遍。
lines.en: I count the stock once, then count it again.

lines.zh: 秤砣在手里，我掂了掂，觉得沉。
lines.en: The weight sits in my palm, heavier than I recall.

lines.zh: 我打开新到的货，闻见铁锈味。
lines.en: I open the new shipment and smell rust.

lines.zh: 门口的铃没响，今天客人不多。
lines.en: The door bell has not rung; few customers today.

lines.zh: 我在修一个破箱子，钉子不够。
lines.en: I mend a broken crate and run short of nails.

lines.zh: 我算了算今天的收益，不多。
lines.en: I tally today's takings; they are modest.

lines.zh: 有块金属我认不出，先放一边。
lines.en: One metal I cannot identify, so I set it aside.

lines.zh: 我拍了拍柜台，把灰拍掉。
lines.en: I pat the counter and knock the dust off.

lines.zh: 我在等补货的时间，它总会到。
lines.en: I wait for restocking time; it always comes.

lines.zh: 我的手指被划了一道，缠上了布。
lines.en: A cut on my finger, wrapped up in cloth.

lines.zh: 店里安静，我听见金属自己响。
lines.en: The shop is quiet, and I hear the metal ringing.

lines.zh: 客人，你手上那块铁，我出价。
lines.en: Customer, that iron in your hand — I will offer.

lines.zh: 我先看你腰间的袋子，不看脸。
lines.en: I look at your belt pouch first, not your face.

lines.zh: 你穿成这样，是来买还是来卖？
lines.en: Dressed like that, are you buying or selling?

lines.zh: 我眯眼看你，估算你值多少。
lines.en: I squint at you and estimate what you are worth.

lines.zh: 你靴底带泥，刚从矿里回来吧。
lines.en: Mud on your soles; you came from the mines.

lines.zh: 别把手放在柜台上，会压坏漆。
lines.en: Do not lean on the counter; you will ruin the varnish.

lines.zh: 我认得你，上次你少给我两块铜。
lines.en: I know you; you shorted me two copper last time.

lines.zh: 你看起来不像有钱，但也许有货。
lines.en: You do not look rich, but you may have goods.

lines.zh: 我的价格很公道，公道得让人心疼。
lines.en: My prices are fair, fair enough to sting.

lines.zh: 我抬头看你，脖子发出轻微的响。
lines.en: I look up at you, and my neck creaks softly.

lines.zh: 你的剑不错，可惜我不收旧货。
lines.en: Fine sword, but I do not take worn goods.

lines.zh: 你站得太近，柜台挡不住你。
lines.en: You stand too close; the counter cannot hold you back.

lines.zh: 我笑的时候，你就该当心价钱。
lines.en: When I smile, that is when you watch the price.

lines.zh: 客人，看可以，别碰。
lines.en: Customer, looking is free. Touching is not.

lines.zh: 你袖口的补丁，说明你常来。
lines.en: The patch on your sleeve says you come here often.

lines.zh: 我先看你的手，再看你的剑。
lines.en: I study your hands before your sword.

lines.zh: 别打！货会掉，账会乱！
lines.en: Do not hit me! Goods fall, accounts scramble!

lines.zh: 我抱着头蹲下，先护住账本。
lines.en: I crouch and cover my head, shielding the ledger first.

lines.zh: 这一下够我修三天柜台。
lines.en: This will cost me three days of counter repairs.

lines.zh: 血滴在价签上，字都看不清了。
lines.en: Blood drips on a price tag and blurs the numbers.

lines.zh: 我退到墙角，那里没有货。
lines.en: I back into the corner, where no stock stands.

lines.zh: 你打断了我的秤，这很贵。
lines.en: You broke my scale. That was expensive.

lines.zh: 疼，但我先算损失。
lines.en: It hurts, but I count the losses first.

lines.zh: 我喊了一声，声音像破铜。
lines.en: I cry out, and it sounds like torn copper.

lines.zh: 别打了，我们可以谈价。
lines.en: Stop hitting me; we can negotiate.

lines.zh: 我这身板，挨两下就该收摊。
lines.en: This frame takes two hits and closes for the day.

lines.zh: 你要拿食物换铁？我不做这生意。
lines.en: Food for iron? I do not do that trade.

lines.zh: 那袋面包不值两块铜，最多一块。
lines.en: That bread is not worth two copper, one at most.

lines.zh: 我闻了闻，食物我不收，会坏。
lines.en: I sniff it; I take no food. It spoils.

lines.zh: 你举这么高，是怕我看不清吗？
lines.en: Holding it that high, afraid I cannot see it?

lines.zh: 我不吃东西，我只称东西。
lines.en: I do not eat things. I weigh them.

lines.zh: 这味道让我想起仓库里烂掉的那箱。
lines.en: That smell recalls a rotten crate in my storeroom.

lines.zh: 吃的你带走，我这店里只有秤。
lines.en: Take the food along; my shop stocks only scales.

lines.zh: 我这里只换金属，别的免谈。
lines.en: I trade only in metal. Nothing else.

lines.zh: 你要是饿了，隔壁也许有人肯换。
lines.en: If you are hungry, someone next door might trade.

lines.zh: 你晃它没用，我的秤不认面包。
lines.en: Waving it will not help; my scale knows no bread.

lines.zh: 小心，我一撞就倒，货也跟着倒。
lines.en: Careful, one bump topples me and the stock.

lines.zh: 你撞到货架，铁锭掉了一地。
lines.en: You hit the shelf, and ingots scatter across the floor.

lines.zh: 我退到柜台后，那里比较安全。
lines.en: I step behind the counter, where it is safer.

lines.zh: 别推，我这把老骨头只有二十五点。
lines.en: Do not shove; this old frame has only twenty-five.

lines.zh: 我们撞在一起，秤砣落地响了很久。
lines.en: We collide, and the weight rings on the floor.

lines.zh: 你身上硬，我这身只是布和铜。
lines.en: You are armored; I am only cloth and copper.

lines.zh: 让一让，你挡住我的通道了。
lines.en: Step aside; you are blocking my aisle.

lines.zh: 撞掉的钉子，等下我自己捡。
lines.en: Nails knocked loose? I will gather them later.

lines.zh: 我这店小，转个身都碰得到东西。
lines.en: The shop is small; I bump things just turning around.

lines.zh: 你再挤，我就把门关上。
lines.en: Push again, and I will close the door.

lines.zh: 我的伴侣，是账本最后一行。
lines.en: My partner is the last line of the ledger.

lines.zh: 我们合伙开店，各记一半的账。
lines.en: We run the shop together, each keeping half the books.

lines.zh: 成对做生意，比成对过日子实在。
lines.en: Partnering in trade is more solid than partnering in life.

lines.zh: 她管进货，我管价钱。
lines.en: She handles the shipments; I handle the prices.

lines.zh: 我们分开多年，账还没算清。
lines.en: We parted years ago, and the accounts still are not settled.

lines.zh: 两个人守一个柜台，只会吵。
lines.en: Two people behind one counter only argue.

lines.zh: 我这辈子只信两样：秤和契约。
lines.en: In my life I trusted two things: scale and contract.

lines.zh: 娶亲要聘礼，我这点家当不够。
lines.en: A bride price? My holdings do not cover it.

lines.zh: 同类见面，先比谁的称准。
lines.en: When kin meet, we compare whose scale is truest.

lines.zh: 我独自看店，早就习惯了。
lines.en: I mind the shop alone, and I am long used to it.

lines.zh: 掉在地上的，先称再谈价。
lines.en: Whatever falls, I weigh before we discuss price.

lines.zh: 这枚铜板滚到柜子底下去了。
lines.en: That copper rolled under the cabinet.

lines.zh: 我弯腰去捡，腰响了一声。
lines.en: I bend to pick it up, and my back clicks.

lines.zh: 掉的东西归店主，这是规矩。
lines.en: Dropped goods belong to the shopkeeper. House rule.

lines.zh: 我把它放回架上，标签还没写。
lines.en: I put it back on the shelf; the tag is not written.

lines.zh: 这锭成色不错，我留下了。
lines.en: This ingot is good quality. I keep it.

lines.zh: 我两只手都占着，先放下账本。
lines.en: Both hands are full; I set the ledger down first.

lines.zh: 我不白捡，我会记上一笔。
lines.en: I do not take for free; I write it down.

lines.zh: 这块铁太轻，我掂着就不对。
lines.en: This iron is too light; it feels wrong in my hand.

lines.zh: 你的东西，掉了也别怪我。
lines.en: If you drop something, do not blame me.

lines.zh: 有人碰了我的货架，我看见了。
lines.en: Someone touched my shelf, and I saw it.

lines.zh: 你不是来买东西的，我闻得出。
lines.en: You are not here to buy; I can smell it.

lines.zh: 我盯上你，因为你一直在看门。
lines.en: I fix on you because you keep eyeing the door.

lines.zh: 那只手伸向锭的时候，我就动了。
lines.en: When that hand reached for the ingot, I moved.

lines.zh: 我记下你的脸，价格会变。
lines.en: I note your face; the price just changed.

lines.zh: 客人可以讲价，不可以拿。
lines.en: Customers may haggle; they may not take.

lines.zh: 你脚步太轻，是怕我听见吧。
lines.en: Your steps are too light. Afraid I would hear?

lines.zh: 我这店小，进来的人我都记得。
lines.en: My shop is small; I remember everyone who enters.

lines.zh: 你腰后鼓起来那块，我看见了。
lines.en: That bulge at your back, I see it.

lines.zh: 我数到三，你把东西放回去。
lines.en: I count to three. Put it back.

lines.zh: 我慢慢挪到门边，把路堵上。
lines.en: I drift toward the door and block the way.

lines.zh: 我的手按在柜台下的东西上。
lines.en: My hand rests on something beneath the counter.

lines.zh: 你往左，我就往左挪半步。
lines.en: You go left, and I shift half a step left.

lines.zh: 别急，我这点血，打起来很短。
lines.en: Do not rush; with this little health, a fight is brief.

lines.zh: 我在算你值多少，不是你能打多少。
lines.en: I am pricing you, not measuring your strength.

lines.zh: 你的手在剑柄上磨来磨去。
lines.en: Your hand keeps rubbing that sword hilt.

lines.zh: 我笑给你看，其实在数你的同伴。
lines.en: I smile at you while counting your companions.

lines.zh: 门口有铃，你跑不了多远。
lines.en: There is a bell at the door; you will not get far.

lines.zh: 我先看你动手，再决定价钱。
lines.en: I will watch you swing, then set the price.

lines.zh: 价格谈不拢，就换个谈法。
lines.en: If the price will not settle, we settle differently.

lines.zh: 我抡起秤砣，砸在你膝上。
lines.en: I swing the scale weight into your knee.

lines.zh: 这不是打架的力气，是搬货的力气。
lines.en: This is not fighting strength; it is hauling strength.

lines.zh: 我打一下就退，站远了才安全。
lines.en: I hit once and retreat; distance is safety.

lines.zh: 你抢我的货，就别怪我拿钳子。
lines.en: Rob my stock and I will use the tongs.

lines.zh: 秤杆打在你手臂上，断了。
lines.en: The scale beam hits your arm and snaps.

lines.zh: 我只有二十五点血，所以先下手。
lines.en: Only twenty-five health, so I strike first.

lines.zh: 这一下不值钱，但很疼。
lines.en: This blow is worthless, but it hurts.

lines.zh: 我砸的是你的手，不是你的头。
lines.en: I aim at your hands, not your head.

lines.zh: 你退了，我就把东西收回柜台。
lines.en: If you retreat, I put the goods back.

lines.zh: 别逼我，我打人不专业。
lines.en: Do not push me; I am no professional fighter.

lines.zh: 我打开店门，把牌子翻到营业。
lines.en: I open the shop and turn the sign to open.

lines.zh: 我把第一批货摆上架，店就算开了。
lines.en: I shelve the first shipment, and the shop is open.

lines.zh: 这间铺子空了很久，我租下了。
lines.en: This shop stood empty a long while; I took it.

lines.zh: 我一来就先去数库存。
lines.en: I arrived and counted the stock first.

lines.zh: 秤挂上墙的那一刻，我算有了家。
lines.en: The day the scale went on the wall, I had a home.

lines.zh: 我生来就会算账，没人教过我。
lines.en: I could keep accounts from birth; no one taught me.

lines.zh: 门口那个铃，是我自己装上的。
lines.en: I hung the door bell myself.

lines.zh: 我先把价签写好，再开门迎客。
lines.en: I write the price tags before I open for trade.

lines.zh: 这堆金属，是我一块块搬进来的。
lines.en: I carried every one of these metals in myself.

lines.zh: 开张那天，一个客人都没有。
lines.en: On opening day, not one customer came.

lines.zh: 火！我这些货里有易燃的！
lines.en: Fire! Some of this stock burns!

lines.zh: 我从梯子上摔下来，铜板撒一地。
lines.en: I fall off the ladder, and coins scatter.

lines.zh: 水漫进店里，货全毁了。
lines.en: Water floods the shop; the stock is ruined.

lines.zh: 气浪把我的招牌吹掉了。
lines.en: The blast tears my sign off the wall.

lines.zh: 箭钉在柜台上，离账本一寸。
lines.en: The arrow sticks in the counter, an inch from the ledger.

lines.zh: 药水味盖过了铁锈味，很难闻。
lines.en: Potion reek drowns the rust smell, and it stinks.

lines.zh: 我忙着看店，忘了吃东西。
lines.en: I was minding the shop and forgot to eat.

lines.zh: 雷劈坏了屋顶，又要花钱。
lines.en: Lightning wrecked the roof. More expense.

lines.zh: 掉下去时，我还攥着账本。
lines.en: As I fall, I am still clutching the ledger.
